title: gpu-occupancy-nsight-run-2026-03-03
content:
Executive summary:

This doc summarizes Nsight profiling runs focused on GPU utilization and occupancy for the production inference path (gpt-like decoder) on our current Dedicated instances (A100-40GB equivalent). Goal was to identify bottlenecks that reduce SM occupancy and increase per-token latency, and evaluate the impact of enabling CUDA Graphs for the request-path.

Key findings (short):
- Sustained SM utilization is low (~28-35%) across long-sequence workloads without KV cache hits; achieved_occupancy for the largest kernels is in the 22-38% range.
- Memory-bound kernels (embedding gather + key/value scatter) show high DRAM throughput but low compute utilization.
- Small kernels (per-step attention softmax, rotary + layernorm fusion) suffer from kernel launch overhead and poor parallelism for short sequences (<=64 tokens).
- Enabling CUDA graphs for the common request-path improved tail latency (p95) by ~12% and reduced kernel launch stalls, but did not change raw occupancy numbers for the large attention matmuls.

Environment and workload:
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100-40GB (driver 535.xx), CUDA 12.2, NCCL 2.18
- Model: 7B decoder-only transformer, fp16, optimized attention kernels (custom fused kernels enabled)
- Batch shapes tested: single-request streaming (batch=1), small batched inference (batch=4), steady throughput (batch=16)
- Sequence lengths: 16, 64, 256, 1024 (to evaluate short vs long context behavior)

Profiling approach and commands used:
- Primary tools: nsight-systems (nsys) for end-to-end timeline, nsight-compute (ncu) for kernel metrics, and CUPTI-backed counters for occupancy.
- Example commands used:
  - nsys profile -o nsys_run_seq256 --trace=cuda,nvtx --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --sample=none ./server --workload seq=256,batch=1
  - ncu --set full --metrics achieved_occupancy,sm_efficiency,sm__warps_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_active,dram_throughput ./server --workload seq=1024,batch=4
  - nvprof is deprecated but old capture: nvprof --print-gpu-trace --metrics achieved_occupancy,warp_efficiency ./server
- We also captured timeline exports (.qdrep/.ncu-rep) uploaded to Confluence for visual inspection.

Representative metrics (seq=256, batch=4, steady-state generation step):
- Attention matmul (fwd, large): duration 1.30 ms, achieved_occupancy 36%, sm_efficiency 32%, dram_throughput 420 GB/s (close to peak) -> memory bandwidth active but low SM efficiency -> memory-bound behavior.
- KV write kernel (scatter): duration 0.48 ms, achieved_occupancy 28%, warp_efficiency 84% -> small grids, limited blocks per SM.
- Fused rotary+layernorm (pointwise): duration 0.12 ms, achieved_occupancy 16%, warp_efficiency 70% -> too few threads per block for long sequences due to launch config tied to token count.
- Softmax (attention normalization): duration 0.08 ms, achieved_occupancy 12%, high active warps but short duration -> kernel launch overhead dominates for short sequences.

Timeline observations (from nsys):
- Frequent short kernels per token create many enqueue/launch events; GPU goes idle between short kernels causing serialization.
- CUDA Graph capture eliminated many launch events when the request logic was stable (single prompt path) but dynamic shapes (variable seq length) prevented graph reuse in ~15% of requests.
- PCIe/CPU-side stalls were visible when host-side batching logic synchronized too often (see timeline region 00:12:34.500 - host_waits).

Bottleneck analysis:
1) Memory-bound matmuls: attention matmul shows high DRAM throughput and modest occupancy. The primary limiter is memory bandwidth and tensor core utilization not fully saturated (likely due to padding/shape fragmentation and non-contiguous memory access for KV layout).
2) Kernel launch overhead and short kernels: many sub-ms kernels incur fixed driver/launch cost; this is most prominent for batch=1 and short sequences.
3) Limited SM occupancy for pointwise kernels: per-thread work is small for certain kernels (layernorm/rotary) and block sizing is suboptimal for sequence length aligned with warp sizes, resulting in low blocks-per-SM.

Actionable recommendations (ordered):
- Increase per-kernel parallelism: tune thread/block configuration for pointwise kernels to ensure more blocks per SM regardless of sequence length (aim for >= 16 blocks/SM where possible).
- Kernel fusion: fuse short, successive pointwise ops (e.g., rotary -> layernorm -> dropout -> residual add) to reduce launches and increase arithmetic intensity. Prior experiments show fused kernels increase achieved_occupancy by ~1.5x for those ops.
- KV layout rework: change KV memory layout to contiguous per-head-major layout to improve coalescing and tensor core utilization. Run small experiment swapping existing layout for head-major and re-profile.
- Enable and expand CUDA Graph usage: capture common fixed-shape paths (prompt-only, token-step path) and implement fallback fast-path for dynamic shapes. Observed improvements: p95 -12%, p99 -8% for stable shape requests.
- Asynchronous host logic: reduce CPU-GPU synchronization points by batching NVTX ranges and deferring host-side reductions where possible. Timeline indicates ~6-10% CPU-side stall time for current host syncs.
- Shared-memory and register tuning: for fused kernels, tune shared memory usage to increase occupancy without spilling. Use ncu's register_usage metrics to find RS (registers per thread) hot spots.
- Consider persistent thread kernels for very short per-token work if fusion is not feasible.

Quick experiments to run (next week):
- Experiment A: Rebuild pointwise kernels with blocks_per_sm tuned and measure achieved_occupancy and p95. (Owner: Ethan)
- Experiment B: Implement head-major KV layout in a branch and run seq=1024, batch=4 reference run; compare dram_throughput and tensor_core_utilization. (Owner: Priya)
- Experiment C: Add CUDA Graph capture/restore for the single-shape token-step path and benchmark tail latency at 99th. (Owner: Maya)

Known limitations of this investigation:
- Profiling overhead: ncu (full) runs add overhead; numbers taken from ncu-attached runs should be interpreted relatively. We used separate nsys traces for latency numbers with lower overhead.
- Model-specific: results are for the current 7B variant with our fused-attention; different model shapes or un-fused kernels may behave differently.
- A100 vs other GPUs: occupancy targets and throughput numbers will differ on other architectures (H100 has different tensor core behaviors).

Attachments and artifacts:
- nsys timeline: google-drive link (see linked_artifacts on Confluence page)
- ncu reports: ncu-report-seq1024.ncu-rep (uploaded)
- nvtx-instrumented server branch: github PR #614

Conclusions:
We have clear opportunities to improve latency and utilization by (1) reducing kernel launch overhead via fusion and CUDA Graphs, (2) increasing occupancy for pointwise kernels via block/thread tuning, and (3) improving KV memory layout to better utilize memory bandwidth and tensor cores. The recommended next step is to prioritize a small experiment set (A/B/C above) and re-profile after each change. If occupancy for large matmuls remains low after layout improvements, we should evaluate alternative kernel implementations (cuBLASGEMM/attention kernels) or tiling strategies.

Notes to reviewers:
- Please review linked GitHub PR for NVTX instrumentation.
- If you have representative production traces (especially variable-length prompt logs), drop them into the Confluence page linked above so we can prioritize which shapes need graph-friendly pathing.
